image_description: A large, white radio telescope dish antenna mounted on a complex steel truss support structure against a clear blue sky. The dish is tilted upwards, revealing the grid-like mesh surface and the sub-reflector assembly suspended above the center by struts. The base includes a rotating mount mechanism.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous parabolic dish antenna of colossal scale, dwarfing all surrounding structures.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly shows a massive parabolic dish that dominates the frame, with trees in the background appearing tiny in comparison, confirming the colossal scale.
The rim of the dish forms a smooth, consistent elliptical projection indicative of a precise parabolic curve viewed at an angle. No warping or irregularities are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Massive installation spanning an area visible from great distances.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the object is large, the 'spanning an area visible from great distances' implies a wider context or multiple units which cannot be fully verified from this single close-up shot, though the scale is implied.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Receiver feed horn at focal point of dish.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A sub-reflector assembly (part of the Cassegrain feed system) is clearly visible suspended above the center of the dish by three struts, positioned at the geometric focal point.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Alt-azimuth or equatorial mount for celestial tracking.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dish is mounted on a heavy-duty trunnion axis allowing elevation movement, attached to a rotating base, characteristic of an alt-azimuth mount used for tracking.
The base structure shows a circular track/rotation mechanism typical for azimuthal rotation.
The lower part of the support structure appears to be anchored into a substantial concrete pier/foundation, although partially obscured by the angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Metal mesh or solid aluminum panel dish surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The underside of the dish reveals a grid pattern, indicating it is constructed from metal mesh or perforated panels, which is standard for radio telescopes to reduce wind load.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Astronomical instrument for detecting radio-frequency emissions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visual features (large dish, feed horn, mount) are exclusively characteristic of a radio telescope.
The robust mechanical joints and motor housings visible on the mount structure are consistent with high-precision celestial tracking equipment.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific type of astronomical instrument and rule out misclassification as a satellite dish or solar concentrator.
To verify the 3D structural integrity of the truss work and ensure the feed horn struts connect logically to the dish rim without melting or floating artifacts.
To check for edge bleeding between the thin struts and the sky, and ensure the mesh texture doesn't dissolve into the background.
To detect any subtle texture anomalies in the sky or unnatural smoothing in the metal surfaces.

focus_areas: Connection points of the feed horn struts to the dish rim
Consistency of the mesh/grid pattern on the dish underside
Structural logic of the truss support system
Edge sharpness against the sky background
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the geometry of the sub-reflector support struts; AI often fails to render these thin, tension-bearing structures correctly, resulting in fusion with the dish or impossible angles. Verify that the mesh pattern remains consistent and does not turn into noise or blur near the edges.
